transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-12 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~48m | Recording: Fireflies AI auto-transcript
Attendees: Sarah (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood SE), David (Avalon), Priya (Avalon PM), Kenji (Procurement), Lucia (Security)

[00:00] Sarah: hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. quick agenda — align on POC success criteria, sizing & benchmarks, and the commercial guardrails (credits, SOW, path to procurement). sound good?
[00:12] David: yes, that works. we mostly want to validate performance on our search rerank and summarization workloads and make sure costs are in line.
[00:20] Priya: and timeline — marketing is aiming for Q3 feature flag so we need an actionable pilot plan.
[00:27] Liam: great. we'll propose a 6-week pilot broken into three phases: baseline runs (week 1), tuning & optimization (weeks 2–4), and acceptance/hand-off (weeks 5–6). baseline will give us p95 latency and cost-per-1M token to compare to your current infra.
[00:45] Kenji: quick, from procurement side — what's typical for credits and pilot terms? we need to know what gets signed and when legal needs to step in.
[00:52] Sarah: good question. for pilots we do a credits-based model — usually a committed credit pool (example: $50k worth of API credits) plus defined token caps and a short SOW. if you exceed the caps we either pause or bill overage at an agreed rate. we can be flexible on the exact amount.
[01:10] Lucia: security also needs to see SOC2, key mgmt integrations and retention policies before we put any PII into the test set.
[01:16] Maya: understood — we'll share SOC2 attestation, our KMS integration notes and default retention 30 days for pilot logs; you can request longer.
[01:24] David: on success criteria — we're thinking: p95 latency under 200ms for short queries, throughput of ~200 qps for the reranker batch window, and quality metrics: >90% agreement on oracle rerank and summarization ROUGE-L delta less than 0.05 versus baseline. is that realistic?
[01:40] Liam: those are reasonable targets to test. couple of caveats: model choice and quantization will change latency and quality tradeoffs. for example, we might test a smaller quantized variant for cost/latency and a full-precision variant for quality. we'll include both in the benchmark suite.
[01:55] Priya: when you say benchmark suite, what's included?
[01:58] Liam: we'll provide a spreadsheet + test harness. spreadsheet columns: test name, sample size, avg tokens, p95 latency, p50, throughput, token cost, quality metrics (precision@k, recall, rouge, embedding recall), and notes. harness will include a script to stream requests at the right QPS and measure end-to-end times.
[02:15] Sarah: and for fairness we'll run a baseline against your current model and an open model (we can run GPT-style open alternatives or a HF hosted model) so you can see cost/quality delta.
[02:25] David: can we also run a short comparative against OpenAI? procurement will ask.
[02:30] Sarah: yes we can arrange that in the benchmark; note that any external provider data transfer constraints need to be accounted for.
[02:36] Kenji: what's the procurement path — do we sign a minimal commercial pilot, or do you need enterprise terms upfront?
[02:42] Sarah: typically a pilot SOW + credit schedule is enough to start. enterprise agreements (SLA, indemnities) usually follow for Dedicated or Private deployments. we'll surface the legal terms that matter in the SOW so proc/legal can triage quickly.
[02:55] Lucia: for security gating — we need encryption at rest with KMS, SAML SSO, and an audit log export we can ingest. also data residency note: our EU customers must stay in eu-west region.
[03:10] Maya: we support region pinning for hosted endpoints and private deployment options for strict residency. audit logs and KMS integrations are supported, we'll include the integration doc link in the packet.
[03:21] David: on workload sizing — our average query is ~60 tokens, peak 450 tokens for long summaries. expected steady-state QPS for rerank is 80 qps, peak bursts to 200 qps for flash sales.
[03:34] Liam: ok we'll size the pool initially for 200 qps burst with autoscaling and also run a prefix/KV cache test since you have repeat prefixes for product descriptions — that usually lowers cost significantly.
[03:45] Priya: can you give a concrete credit example? we need to put numbers to this for procurement.
[03:50] Sarah: example pilot: $40k credit, 6 weeks. Allocate $20k to benchmark runs (high-volume blasts to characterize latency & throughput), $15k to iterative tuning and real traffic shadowing, $5k reserved for overages or a short extended run. If you hit 80% consumption by week 4 we can reevaluate top-up.
[04:08] Kenji: and the invoices or credits — do we need a PO or is an MSA required straight away?
[04:12] Sarah: for pilots we can accept a PO for credits in most cases; MSA can be signed later if you opt to go to enterprise. Kenji: Procurement tends to want an MSA up front. We'll provide a redlineable SOW and a reference MSA that covers minimal terms.
[04:26] David: what about acceptance criteria — how do we sign off?
[04:29] Liam: acceptance is metric driven: agreed thresholds on latency/throughput + quality thresholds. we'll run the final benchmark on production-ish traffic or on the provided sample and produce a results report. if thresholds are met, we consider pilot successful and then discuss committed capacity or pricing.
[04:45] Priya: example quality thresholds?
[04:47] Liam: for rerank: NDCG@10 delta less than 0.02 vs baseline, precision@5 within 0.03 and embedding recall >0.85. For summarization: ROUGE-L within 0.05. We'll formalize these in the SOW.
[05:02] Lucia: any data retention during pilot? you mentioned 30 days, will that be shorter if we ask?
[05:07] Maya: yes for pilots we can set retention to 7 days on request and exclude logs that contain PII — or we can provide a redaction pre-processing step in the harness.
[05:18] David: ok, show of hands — do we want Dedicated for pilot?
[05:21] Priya: Dedicated might be overkill for pilot cost wise — we prefer hosted with region pinning if possible.
[05:26] Sarah: agree, hosted pinned to eu-west is our recommended fast path. Dedicated reserved capacity is usually a follow-up when you need hard SLOs.
[05:33] Kenji: I want to understand acceptance to procurement hand-off — if pilot successful what is typical ramp timeline to enterprise contract?
[05:39] Sarah: usually 4–8 weeks for procurement and legal review once you commit to Dedicated. Negotiation times can vary; we'll prepare a minimal enterprise term sheet to accelerate that.
[05:48] Priya: any limitations we should know about the test harness? for example streaming endpoints or function calls?
[05:52] Liam: we support streaming and function/tool calling. the harness will run both sync generation and streaming to measure end-to-end latency. sometimes transcription or auto-chunking in the transcript can mis-label the streaming overhead, so we'll annotate that in the results.
[06:08] Sarah: we'll also indicate model variants and quantization levels for each test row so you can map cost vs latency vs quality.
[06:15] David: what's the rollback/fallback if production traffic starts to degrade?
[06:19] Maya: Redwood supports automated fallback policies — route to a smaller model variant or a cached response, and we have canary deploys for rollouts. we'll document this in the runbook.
[06:28] Kenji: on the contract side — I need an explicit clause about pilot liabilities and data handling. do you have a standard pilot addendum?
[06:34] Sarah: yes we typically include a one-page pilot addendum that covers scope, credit limits, data handling for pilot, termination, and a short liability cap. we'll attach that to the SOW.
[06:44] Priya: timeline check — if SOW is out by Fri (2025-03-14) and we provide samples by Mon (2025-03-17) can we kick baseline the following week?
[06:52] Sarah: yes that's reasonable. so tentative baseline week starting 2025-03-24.
[06:58] David: splendid.
[07:00] Sarah: okay let's recap next steps. we'll send the SOW with example credit structure, the benchmark spreadsheet and harness, SOC2/KMS docs and a redlineable MSA reference. you (David) will share sample queries and traffic profile; Kenji will coordinate PO/ procurement timing; Lucia will review security docs.
[07:18] Priya: quick question — pricing after pilot, do you have committed capacity discounts?
[07:22] Sarah: yes we have reserved capacity discounts for Dedicated and tiered usage pricing for hosted. we'll include indicative pricing bands in the SOW for forecasting.
[07:30] David: competitors — will the benchmark compare to OpenAI?
[07:33] Liam: yes, if you want. we'll include a comparative row but will surface differences in prompt engineering and tokenization that can skew raw token metrics.
[07:44] Kenji: final ask — please include an explicit expiration on the credit offer and who signs it.
[07:49] Sarah: will do. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the packet.
[07:54] Lucia: thanks.
[07:56] David: great meeting.
